OpenAI is no longer just building models. Now it deploys them too.

This week OpenAI launched a Deployment Company — a new entity backed by 19 partner firms — and acquired Tomoro, adding 150 forward-deployed engineers. The goal is clear: own the path from frontier AI model to enterprise production.

This is a structural change in how AI reaches business. Until now, companies built their own implementation teams or hired consultants to bridge the gap between model and workflow. OpenAI just collapsed that boundary. It is inserting itself between its models and your operations — the exact position where switching costs compound and margins concentrate.

For CTOs, the calculus shifts. When your model provider is also your deployment partner, every integration deepens dependency. For consulting firms and systems integrators, this is a direct incursion into their core business from the model layer.

The signal for the broader market: AI companies are moving downstream. They are not waiting for enterprises to figure out implementation. They are owning it.
